Mario Lemieux, known as The Magnificent One, is a Canadian centre regarded as the second-greatest player in hockey history behind only Gretzky. He won two Stanley Cups with the Pittsburgh Penguins and achieved remarkable scoring consistency despite a career interrupted by injuries and illness.

He scored six hundred ninety goals and one thousand thirty-three assists for one thousand seven hundred twenty-three career points, the third-highest total in NHL history. Lemieux won the Hart Trophy for MVP three times and the Lester B. Pearson Award, then called the Dodge Cup, six times as the players' choice for best player. He led the Pittsburgh Penguins to back-to-back Stanley Cups in nineteen ninety-one and nineteen ninety-two, transforming the franchise from league doormat to dynasty.

He battled Hodgkin's lymphoma during his prime in nineteen eighty-nine to nineteen ninety. Remarkably, he returned to play and was named team captain while recovering from cancer treatment. Lemieux was known for extraordinary size at six feet four inches, reach, and skill. He could score using either hand and possessed elite playmaking ability. He won the Canada Cup in nineteen eighty-seven in a legendary performance on the world stage, cementing his status as a national hero. He briefly served as owner of the Penguins from nineteen ninety-nine to two thousand five, becoming the only player to own an NHL team.
